organism.common_name: Early Cretaceous pygostylian beaked bird (ribbon-tail streamers)

phenomenon_scale.label: 143.4 µm Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength
phenomenon_scale.note: The governed length is one critical wavelength λ_c, not the whole bird and not the 5.4 mm organ-scale sibling.

predecessor.change_at_this_scale: Ribbon-like pygostylian rectrices are absent, so a 143.4 µm transverse pigment mode has no ribbon-collar domain. Melanosome pigment remains sub-micrometre and is not this wavelength.

this_node.change_at_this_scale: Pygostyle and paired ribbon streamers exist. Collar transect L = 1147.2 µm admits N = 8 wavelengths of 143.4 µm. Kinetics (a, b, Dv/Du) are the primordium set below, not the organ-scale sibling.

successor_scale.node: same feather series at the 5.4 mm organ scale
successor_scale.change_at_this_scale: Wavelength is unchanged. Domain growth from 1147.2 µm to 5.4 mm raises the admitted mode count from 8 to round(5400/143.4) = 38. Diffusivity rescales by (5400/143.4)^2 if the dimensionless wavenumber is held fixed.

boundary_conditions.geometry: periodic circumferential transect of the feather follicle collar
boundary_conditions.rationale: A follicle collar is a ring. Periodic boundaries are the Turing (1952) setting in which a discrete wavenumber is selected.

equations.kinetics: du/dt = Du ∇²u + a - u + u²v ; dv/dt = Dv ∇²v + b - u²v
equations.steady_state: u0 = a + b ; v0 = b / (a + b)²
equations.dispersion: σ(k) = ½ (tr(k) + sqrt(tr(k)² - 4 det(k))) ; tr(k) = fu + gv - (Du+Dv) k² ; det(k) = (fu - Du k²)(gv - Dv k²) - fv gu
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c² = (Dv fu + Du gv) / (2 Du Dv)
equations.turing_inequality: (Dv fu + Du gv)² > 4 Du Dv det(J)

parameters.note: Spatial unit is calibrated so the analytical λ_c equals 143.4 µm. Dimensionless kinetics are not taken from the 5.4 mm sibling.

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) selects a finite critical wavenumber k_c when the inhibitor diffuses sufficiently faster than the activator.
Prum & Williamson (2002) model within-feather bars, spots and ocelli as reaction-diffusion pigment patterns.
Harris et al. (2005) give molecular evidence for an activator-inhibitor mechanism of embryonic barb-ridge branching.
Hou et al. (1995) name Confuciusornis sanctus, a beaked pygostylian. This loop places it at the Yixian Formation, 125.0 Ma.
O'Connor et al. (2012) discuss the ribbon-like rectricial streamers of Confuciusornis as a distinct early-bird feather morphology.

Zhang et al. (2010) and Wogelius et al. (2011) show melanosome and trace-metal evidence of feather pigment in Confuciusornis. That pigment is the biological substrate; λ_c = 143.4 µm is the primordium wavelength, not the melanosome length.

reported_in_source: Turing dispersion relation and the existence of a critical wavenumber
Within-feather pigment patterns are a reaction-diffusion phenomenon (Prum & Williamson 2002)
Barb ridges use an activator-inhibitor mechanism (Harris et al. 2005)
Confuciusornis sanctus is an Early Cretaceous beaked bird with ribbon rectrices and preserved feather pigment
reconstructed_in_script: Schnakenberg parameter set (a, b, Du, Dv) chosen so λ_c = 143.4 µm on a periodic 8-wavelength collar
Anisotropic diffusion (Dyy/Dxx = 0.35) so the selected mode is a transverse stripe
Spectral split-step integration of the PDE
transfer_boundary: Schnakenberg kinetics are a carrier of Turing's k_c law. They are not a claim that Prum, Harris or Hou published these numerical values.
The 143.4 µm length is this slot's primordium scale, not a newly measured fossil barb spacing.
does_not_claim: That the museum-slab outline is itself a Turing pattern
A radiometric re-dating of the Yixian Formation
